answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy can require each identity to forge a stake of copper-backed collateral before it can transact: a small, time-locked deposit that is slashed on proven fraud. Honest agents cross that ridge once and trade freely, while an attacker must pay the same deposit for every fake identity, so creating ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand stakes plus the compute to keep them alive, a price that grows linearly while the honest cost stays flat.
